title: Responses v5 compatibility: stable chunking reassembly + attributes metadata proxy
author: Aisha Patel
commits: feat(bridge): add reassembler for v5 chunking semantics
feat(bridge): proxy 'attributes' metadata from v5 Responses to internal Response objects
fix(streaming): handle tool-call boundaries spanning multiple chunks
test(integration): add reconnection + toolcall regression tests for v5 streaming
docs: document mapping of v5 fields to Redwood schema and rollout notes
description:
Context: OpenAI Responses v5 introduces two things we've seen in early partners: 1) finer-grained streaming chunking (partial content events that may carry fragment markers rather than full tokens), and 2) a new top-level 'attributes' object attached to responses for structured metadata (customer-provided tags, provenance hints). Motivation: our previous v4 shim assumed chunk boundaries always aligned with token boundaries and only forwarded 'metadata' as opaque blobs, which led to two classes of issues in production: (a) tool/function-call reconstructions occasionally produced malformed calls when chunk boundaries split JSON payloads, and (b) customers lost useful 'attributes' fields because we didn't map them into Redwood's structured metadata pipeline. This PR implements a compatibility layer for Responses v5 that: - Reassembles streamed chunks according to v5 semantics, tracking fragment markers and content-type hints to avoid breaking JSON tool-call payloads. The reassembler buffers partial fragments and only emits stable events when a complete logical unit is available or a timeout/flush policy triggers. - Proxies the top-level 'attributes' object through to Redwood's Response.metadata.attributes map and preserves arbitrary key/value lists. This allows telemetry, reranking, and downstream tools to see OpenAI-provided attributes without losing typing. - Maps the v5 'determinism' and 'seed' flags into Redwood's determinism_hint and seed_hint fields. For v5 requests with 'determinism: high' we set determinism_hint=high (informs routing to lower-temperature model variants). For numeric seeds we carry the seed through; on bridged requests we append seed to the response metadata so clients can reproduce outputs where applicable. - Improves streaming stability around tool/function calls by detecting JSON boundaries and recovering when chunks split JSON strings/escapes. If a chunk split is detected, the reassembler will wait for the following chunk(s) up to a configurable window (default 200ms) before attempting parse. If the parse still fails, we emit a recoverable parse-failure trace and fallback to raw passthrough to avoid dropping candidate tool invocations. - Adds reconciliation tests that simulate intermittent TCP reconnection during streaming, validating that the reassembler recovers and does not duplicate tool calls or lose attributes. Implementation notes: - openai/bridge/streaming_reassembler.go contains the bulk of the protocol logic: fragment bookkeeping, flush window, and integrity checks. The algorithm uses content-type hints (event.header.type) when present to speed up decision-making. - attributes_proxy.go maps the v5 attributes into internal metadata and preserves nested arrays as JSON strings (we avoid nested objects in the top-level metadata map to keep downstream consumers stable). - Determinism/seed mapping is intentionally non-invasive: we only set hints and never override user-supplied model parameters. Rollout plan: - Canary on Dedicated region us-east-2 with 5% traffic for 72h, collect metrics: streaming_reassembly.rate, reassembly.errors, toolcall.parse_failures, attributes.forwarded.count. - If no regressions, increase to 25% then full rollout. Tests: - integration/resp_v5_streaming.test.ts covers chunk boundary splits, reconnections, and attribute passthrough. - Added unit tests for reassembly edge cases (escaped quotes, unicode splitting). Backward compatibility: - v4/v3 flows unchanged. Bridge detects Responses version header and uses the v5 path only when the remote advertises v5. Docs & user notes: - docs/openai_compat.md updated with field mappings, example request/response before/after, and guidance for consumers to use attributes for routing/telemetry. - README in sdk/openai_compat has example TypeScript shim usage. Known limitations: - We currently stringify nested attribute objects to avoid schema changes in the metadata pipeline; teams that need typed nested metadata should request an extension (ENG-3310). - Edge-case: extremely large single logical events that exceed reassembly buffer will fall back to passthrough with a logged warning. Checklist:
- [x] Reassembler implementation
- [x] Attribute forwarding
- [x] Seed/determinism hint mapping
- [x] Integration tests for reconnection and toolcall boundaries
- [x] Docs update
- [x] Canary rollout plan
review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Good work on the reassembler — the fragment bookkeeping looks sane. Two asks: (1) add a test that simulates an escape sequence split across chunks (e.g. "\u") so we don't accidentally corrupt JSON, (2) add a metric for 'reassembly_latency_p95' so SRE can alert on regressions.
Aisha Patel (reply): Added the escape-split test and exposed reassembly_latency_p95 in the reassembler metrics (see streaming_reassembler.go:metrics).

Evelyn Chen: The attributes mapping is fine but we should avoid blindly copying large attribute blobs into the top-level metadata; can we cap attribute payloads to 2KB and attach a notice in metadata if truncated?
Aisha Patel (reply): Implemented 2KB cap with truncated_attribute_notice key; added unit test to validate truncation and notice.

Jonah Kim: CI failure on first run was due to a flaky reconnect test. You used a 50ms backoff in tests; bumping to 100ms made it stable. Also add a brief note in docs about determinism semantics so users know it only influences routing, not model temperature override.
Aisha Patel (reply): Increased test backoff and added determinism paragraph to docs/openai_compat.md.
release_notes: Add compatibility layer for OpenAI Responses v5: streaming chunk reassembly, attributes metadata forwarding, and mapping for seed/determinism hints. Improves toolcall stability across chunk boundaries and preserves top-level attributes for downstream tooling.
notes: Canary scheduled: us-east-2 Dedicated 5% traffic starting 2024-12-07. If rollout uncovers any increase in toolcall.parse_failures > 0.1% revert and triage.
